key_insight: Steric and solvation control enables hybrid perovskite monolayers exceeding 1000 μm² in lateral area, supporting lithography-free, low-static-power optoelectronics.
engineering_relevance: Large ultrathin crystals permit solvent-free contacts through physical shadow masks, avoiding solvent-induced degradation associated with conventional lithography.
method: Use a ternary-solvent growth strategy combining alcohol cosolvents with an amine additive to suppress out-of-plane stacking.
Tune alcohol chain length and solvent volatility to reorganize precursor solvation and sustain edge-mediated transport during annealing.
Fabricate planar devices from isolated ultrathin (PEA)₂PbI₄ channels using physical shadow masking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports applicability across multiple spacers, metals and halides, with device dark currents of 10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹³ A, approximately 0.2 pW static power at 5 V—250-fold below drop-cast films—and a light-to-dark current ratio of 430.
watch_item: Wafer-scale coverage, device-to-device reproducibility and long-term operational stability are not established in the abstract.
paper_title: Universal Synthesis of Large-Area Hybrid Perovskite Monolayers Enabling Lithography-Free, Low-Static-Power Optoelectronics
